title: Tdap / Td: routine and catch-up intervals
summary: After a completed primary series, give one Tdap if never received, then Td or Tdap every 10 years. An incomplete series uses Tdap, Td/Tdap ≥4 weeks later, then Td/Tdap 6–12 months later.
population: Adults with incomplete or unknown tetanus/pertussis history.
locator: Tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis — routine vaccination
evidenceNote: CDC schedule; recommendation-specific certainty not extracted.
cautions: Pregnancy and wound management have separate timing. Review prior doses; do not restart a completed series.

title: RSV: age and risk eligibility
summary: Give one RSV vaccine dose at age ≥75, or age 50–74 with increased severe-RSV risk. It is not an annual vaccine; do not repeat a previous dose under this guidance.
population: Adults ≥75; adults 50–74 with guideline-defined risk.
locator: Recommendations; number of doses; risk conditions
evidenceNote: No separate certainty grade extracted from this CDC guidance.
cautions: Review the full risk-condition list and vaccine precautions. Pregnancy is a separate pathway.

title: Pneumococcal: risk-based vaccination before age 50
summary: At age 19–49 with a qualifying risk condition and no prior pneumococcal vaccine, use PCV20/PCV21 alone or PCV15 followed by PPSV23, usually ≥1 year later.
population: Adults 19–49 with diabetes, specified chronic disease, smoking, or other listed risks.
locator: Adults 19 through 49 — never received vaccine; risk conditions
evidenceNote: CDC risk-based schedule; no separate certainty grade extracted.
cautions: Minimum PPSV23 interval may be 8 weeks with immunocompromise, CSF leak or cochlear implant. Prior doses and regional serotype 4 risk alter choices. Hypertension alone is not chronic-heart-disease eligibility.

title: RZV: immunocompromised adults ≥19
summary: Use two RZV doses, usually 2–6 months apart. A 1–2 month interval can be used when earlier completion before more intense immunosuppression would help.
population: Adults ≥19 who are or will be immunodeficient or immunosuppressed due to disease or treatment.
evidenceNote: Guidance supplements the 2022 ACIP policy; separate certainty not extracted.
cautions: Coordinate with the treating specialist. Review varicella history, precautions, and prior-dose timing; this is not an individualized schedule.

title: COVID-19: current seasonal schedule review
summary: CDC’s September 2026 page recommends a 2026–2027 vaccine for adults ≥18; dose count and interval depend on age, product, history and immune status. Use its current tables for scheduling.
population: Adults considering 2026–2027 COVID-19 vaccination.
evidenceNote: No single recommendation-level certainty grade extracted; source date discrepancy is explicitly retained for review.
cautions: Automatic dose matching is withheld: the page retains an inconsistent table-heading date, and identifies some uses as off-label. Immunocompromised schedules are separate.

title: Colorectal screening: age 45–49
summary: Offer colorectal cancer screening starting at age 45.
population: Asymptomatic average-risk adults aged 45–49.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Options include annual FIT or colonoscopy every 10 years. Abnormal non-colonoscopy tests need colonoscopy. High-risk histories need separate pathways.

title: Colorectal screening: age 50–75
summary: Screen adults aged 50–75. Annual FIT and colonoscopy every 10 years are two recommended strategies.
population: Asymptomatic average-risk adults aged 50–75.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Match modality to preferences and follow-up capacity; abnormal stool tests require colonoscopy.

title: Colorectal screening: individualized age 76–85
summary: Selectively offer screening at ages 76–85 using health, prior screening and preferences.
population: Average-risk adults aged 76–85.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Previously unscreened adults may benefit more. Routine screening stops after 85.

title: Breast screening: biennial mammography
summary: Screen every two years from age 40 through 74.
population: Women and other people assigned female at birth at average breast-cancer risk.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Prior breast cancer, high-risk lesions, pathogenic variants or high-dose chest radiation need separate pathways. Evidence is insufficient for routine screening at ≥75 or supplemental imaging solely for dense breasts.

title: Cervical screening: final USPSTF intervals
summary: At age 21–29, use cytology every 3 years. At age 30–65, use cytology every 3 years, primary high-risk HPV every 5 years, or cotesting every 5 years.
population: Average-risk people with a cervix, age 21–65.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: This is the 2018 final statement, not the 2024 draft. Prior CIN2+, cancer, immunocompromise or DES exposure needs individualized surveillance; do not apply average-risk exit criteria.

title: Lung screening: annual low-dose CT
summary: Screen annually at age 50–80 with ≥20 pack-years and current smoking or quitting within 15 years.
population: Asymptomatic adults meeting all USPSTF age and smoking criteria.
locator: Recommendation summary; screening interval and stopping criteria
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Stop after 15 years without smoking, or if health limits life expectancy or ability/willingness for curative lung surgery. Include shared decision-making and cessation support.

title: AAA: one-time ultrasound after smoking
summary: Offer one-time abdominal ultrasound to men aged 65–75 who have ever smoked.
population: Asymptomatic men age 65–75; ever smoking commonly means ≥100 lifetime cigarettes.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Family history and other risks still matter. Women have separate Grade D or I pathways; this record does not apply to them.

title: AAA: selective screening without smoking
summary: Selectively offer one-time ultrasound after considering family history, other risks and preferences.
population: Asymptomatic men age 65–75 who never smoked.
locator: Recommendation summary — men who never smoked
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: The small average benefit does not support automatically screening everyone in this group.

title: PSA screening: shared decision at age 55–69
summary: Decide individually about periodic PSA screening after discussion of benefits, false positives, overdiagnosis and treatment harms.
population: Men aged 55–69 without prostate-cancer symptoms.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Do not screen someone who does not prefer screening after discussion. Family history and other risk factors inform the discussion; no universal interval is assigned here.

title: PSA screening: age ≥70
summary: Do not routinely use PSA-based screening in men aged 70 or older.
population: Asymptomatic men aged ≥70.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: This concerns screening, not evaluation of symptoms or surveillance after a cancer diagnosis.

title: HIV screening: routine and increased risk
summary: Screen at age 15–65; screen outside that range when risk is increased. Screen every pregnancy, including labor/delivery if status is unknown.
population: Adolescents and adults without a known HIV diagnosis.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Repeat screening is reasonable with ongoing risk; USPSTF has not established one optimal repeat interval.

title: HCV screening: age 18–79
summary: Screen once for most adults aged 18–79 using antibody testing with confirmatory HCV RNA.
population: Asymptomatic adults 18–79 without known liver disease.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Repeat testing with continuing exposure risk; no single optimal repeat interval is established. High-risk people outside the age range may also merit testing.

title: HBV screening: CDC universal triple panel
summary: Screen adults ≥18 at least once with HBsAg, anti-HBs and total anti-HBc.
population: Adults not previously screened with the complete triple panel.
locator: CDC recommendations — universal screening of adults
evidenceNote: CDC recommendation; no USPSTF grade or ACC/AHA level substituted.
cautions: Periodic risk-based testing and pregnancy screening are separate. Vaccination does not replace recommended screening; interpret all three results together.

title: Latent TB: screen increased-risk adults
summary: Screen asymptomatic adults at increased risk, including birth/former residence in high-prevalence countries or high-risk congregate settings.
population: Adults ≥18 at increased LTBI risk, without active-TB symptoms.
locator: Clinician summary — assessment of risk and frequency
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Use IGRA or TST; IGRA has advantages after BCG vaccination. Repeat frequency depends on exposure risk. Positive tests require evaluation to exclude active TB before LTBI treatment.

title: Chlamydia and gonorrhea: age and risk
summary: Screen sexually active women age ≤24, and women ≥25 with increased infection risk, using NAAT.
population: Asymptomatic sexually active women, including pregnant persons.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Consider anatomy and exposure sites. USPSTF evidence is insufficient for routine screening in men; CDC has additional population-specific screening recommendations.

title: Syphilis screening: increased risk
summary: Screen asymptomatic nonpregnant adolescents and adults at increased risk.
population: Risk assessment includes exposures, local epidemiology and other STIs.
locator: Clinician summary — risk assessment and interval
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: MSM or people with HIV may benefit from at least annual testing, or every 3–6 months with continuing high risk. Pregnancy and symptomatic disease need separate pathways.

title: After 1–2 small tubular adenomas
summary: Repeat colonoscopy in 7–10 years after complete removal of 1–2 tubular adenomas <10 mm at a high-quality exam.
population: Average-risk adults after high-quality, complete colonoscopy.
evidenceNote: Moderate-quality evidence in the original table; no ACC/AHA equivalent assigned.
cautions: Hereditary syndromes, IBD, prior CRC, malignant polyps or CRC family history require separate assessment.

title: After an adenoma ≥10 mm
summary: Repeat colonoscopy in 3 years after complete removal of an adenoma ≥10 mm at a high-quality exam.
population: Average-risk adults; complete resection and adequate bowel preparation confirmed.
evidenceNote: High-quality evidence in the original table; no ACC/AHA equivalent assigned.
cautions: Piecemeal resection of lesions ≥20 mm needs an earlier pathway. Pathology, examination quality and other history can shorten intervals.

title: Colonoscopy after curative CRC resection
summary: After perioperative clearing, perform surveillance colonoscopy at 1 year; if no neoplasia, next at 3 years, then 5 years, then every 5 years while benefit persists.
population: Adults after curative colorectal cancer resection.
locator: Surveillance intervals after CRC resection — recommendations 2 and 3
evidenceNote: Low-quality evidence for these colonoscopic surveillance recommendations.
cautions: Intervals are measured from the preceding surveillance exam. Lynch syndrome, polyps and rectal-cancer local surveillance alter the plan. This is not the full oncology follow-up schedule.

title: After CIN2+ treatment: HPV-based surveillance
summary: After CIN2+ treatment, obtain negative HPV tests or cotests at 6, 18 and 30 months before spacing to every 3 years; continue long-term surveillance for at least 25 years.
population: People treated for high-grade cervical precancer.
locator: Clarification of post-treatment surveillance; corrected Figure 7
evidenceNote: 2023 update clarifies timing; no separate new evidence grade is inferred.
cautions: Prior results, histology, treatment and immune status determine management. Abnormal follow-up results need the full ASCCP pathway. This is not routine average-risk screening.

title: Osteoporosis screening before age 65
summary: Screen postmenopausal women younger than 65 when clinical risk assessment identifies increased fracture risk.
population: Postmenopausal women <65 without known osteoporosis or secondary causes.
locator: Recommendation summary — postmenopausal women younger than 65
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: First assess risk factors, then use a risk tool if indicated. A universal FRAX screening cutoff is not specified by USPSTF.

title: Osteopenia: U.S. FRAX treatment thresholds
summary: Consider treatment for osteopenia at the femoral neck or total hip when 10-year U.S. FRAX risk is ≥3% for hip fracture or ≥20% for major osteoporotic fracture.
population: Postmenopausal women and men ≥50; appropriate U.S. FRAX model.
evidenceNote: Separate recommendation-level certainty not extracted; no ACC/AHA equivalent assigned.
cautions: These are treatment thresholds, not a USPSTF screening cutoff. FRAX is externally calculated; assess secondary causes and individual context.

title: Hip/vertebral fracture or osteoporosis-range BMD
summary: Consider pharmacologic therapy after hip or vertebral fracture regardless of BMD, or with DXA T-score ≤−2.5 at guideline-specified sites.
population: Postmenopausal women and men ≥50.
evidenceNote: Separate recommendation-level certainty not extracted; no ACC/AHA equivalent assigned.
cautions: Exclude secondary bone disease; renal function, drug safety and fracture risk guide selection.

title: Weight-management medication: BMI and comorbidity
summary: ACP suggests semaglutide or tirzepatide with lifestyle measures as first-line medication at BMI ≥30, or BMI ≥27 to <30 with specified weight-related comorbidity.
population: Nonpregnant adults in outpatient care; comorbidities include diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, OSA or CVD.
evidenceNote: Moderate-certainty evidence for semaglutide and tirzepatide; no ACC/AHA level substituted.
cautions: Assess contraindications, preferences and access. Guideline eligibility does not establish FDA indication, VA formulary status or authorization. Other options have separate rankings.

title: Bariatric surgery: society eligibility thresholds
summary: ASMBS/IFSO recommends surgery at BMI ≥35 regardless of comorbidity. Consider surgery at BMI 30–34.9 with metabolic disease or inadequate durable response to nonsurgical care.
population: Adults evaluated by a multidisciplinary metabolic/bariatric service.
locator: Major updates; class I and class II obesity; conclusions
evidenceNote: No recommendation-specific evidence grade extracted; original society guidance is not an ACC/AHA class.
cautions: Asian-population thresholds are lower. Clinical guideline eligibility differs from insurer or VA program approval; assess operative risk and long-term follow-up.

title: Physical activity: weekly adult targets
summary: Aim for 150–300 minutes of moderate or 75–150 minutes of vigorous aerobic activity weekly, plus muscle strengthening on ≥2 days.
population: Adults able to participate safely; adapt to health and function.
locator: Key guidelines for adults and older adults
evidenceNote: No single recommendation-specific certainty grade extracted from the federal key-guidelines summary.
cautions: Some activity is better than none. Older adults also need balance work; chronic disease may require an individualized plan.

title: Heart-healthy nutrition: the 2026 AHA pattern
summary: Emphasize varied produce, whole grains, plant-rich proteins and unsaturated fats; reduce sodium, added sugar and ultraprocessed food. Do not start alcohol for heart health.
population: Adults pursuing cardiovascular risk reduction.
locator: Nine features of a heart-healthy dietary pattern
evidenceNote: Scientific statement; no recommendation-specific class or evidence level assigned.
cautions: Adapt to culture, food access, energy needs and relevant disease-specific restrictions. This statement does not prescribe one universal meal plan.

title: Tobacco cessation: counseling and medication
summary: Ask about tobacco, advise stopping, and offer behavioral support plus FDA-approved cessation medication to nonpregnant adults who use tobacco.
population: Nonpregnant adults who use tobacco.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: Pregnancy has a separate behavioral-intervention recommendation and insufficient pharmacotherapy evidence. E-cigarettes are not an established cessation intervention in this statement.

title: Alcohol: screen and provide brief counseling
summary: Screen adults ≥18 for unhealthy alcohol use and offer brief behavioral counseling for risky or hazardous use.
population: Adults in primary care, including pregnancy.
evidenceNote: Original USPSTF grade retained; no ACC/AHA evidence level assigned.
cautions: AUDIT-C or a brief single-question screen can be used. A positive screen requires assessment; no universal repeat interval or safe alcohol intake is inferred.
